key: And Joshua said unto Achan: ‘My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make confession unto Him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide nothing from me.’
s: Joshua addresses Achan, singled out as the thief of the devoted thing, before he and all he has are stoned and burned; Radak, on Joshua 7:19, reads the plea as asking confession so that his death atone for his sin and Israel acknowledge the lot.

evidence.words: בקש ממנו שיתודה על עונו לשני דברים האחד לכפרת עונו שתהא מיתתו כפרתו בהודאת עונו ומכאן למדנו שכל המומתין מתודין ולמדו כי כופר עונו מדכתיב יעכרך ה' ביום הזה ביום הזה נעכר ולא לעולם הבא והשני כדי שיודו בני ישראל בגורל או בקליטת הארון ויאמרו כי אמת הוא
evidence.gloss: He asked him to confess his sin for two things: the first, for the atonement of his sin, that his death be his atonement through confessing his sin, and from this we learn that all who are put to death confess; and they learned that his sin was atoned from “the LORD shall trouble thee this day”: this day he is troubled and not in the world to come; the second, so that the children of Israel would acknowledge the lot, or the ark’s catching him, and say that it is true.

reason: verse.js ok, ref Joshua 7:19 and at [193,19] match. Plain sense faithful to Joshua 7: Achan is taken by lot (7:16 to 18) as the one who took of the devoted thing (7:1, 7:11, 7:15), and after his confession he is stoned and burned with all that he had (7:24 to 25); the hard clause is stated plainly, no four-word run from the verse. Read the whole Joshua 7 packet (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David; the Midrash Rabbah has no Joshua volume). Radak on בני שים נא כבוד לה׳ gives exactly two purposes of the requested confession: atonement, his death becoming his atonement through confession, and Israel’s acknowledging the lot (or the ark’s catching him) as true. The sentence carries both without addition; Rashi on the same verse reads it instead as Joshua asking Achan not to defame the lots, which does not contradict the attribution to Radak. Evidence copied verbatim from packet output as one contiguous span (the proposer’s basis had an ellipsis). entry-check ok.
